CRAN submission roadmap

Source: CRAN-ROADMAP.md

Status as of 2026-10-13, from R CMD check --as-cran on R 4.4.2.

Before (decomposer 0.2.0) Now (shapleydecomp 0.3.0)
ERROR 1: package name conflicts with DecomposeR 0
WARNING 1: all 17 exports undocumented, no man/ 0 from the package (qpdf missing on the cluster host only)
NOTE 3: non-standard top-level dirs, undeclared globals, getS3method not imported 1: “new submission”, plus site URLs until the site is deployed
Examples / tests / vignettes none / OK / none OK / OK / OK

1. Blockers

1.1 Package name: resolved

CRAN compares package names case-insensitively, and DecomposeR is already on CRAN, so decomposer / decomposeR would have been refused. The package is now shapleydecomp, in the GitHub repo aucarter/shapleydecomp, and the main entry point is shapley_decompose(), which no longer masks stats::decompose(). The incoming-feasibility name check now passes.

Callers outside this repo still use the old name. They keep working because they load the installed decomposer 0.2.0 build, and each needs moving when it next takes an update: - leapfrog_adulthiv: r_libs.lock pins decomposer 0.2.0, and R/decomp_structural.R calls decomposer::. Install a shapleydecomp build with install_pinned(), bump the lockfile, and replace decomposer:: and decompose( in the same commit. - hiv_decomp/R/adapters/*.R: decomposer::CF_TOTAL_IMPACT and the related constants. - manuscript/main.tex: \pkg{decomposer} throughout.

1.2 Deploy the site so its URLs resolve: done

Live at https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/ since 2026-10-13. The R-CMD-check workflow passed on all five platforms (macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu on devel / release / oldrel-1) at ddd2957.

2. Done on the pkgdown-site branch

  • Roxygen generates man/ and NAMESPACE. All 17 exports are documented, the four .default methods are registered with S3method(), and data.table / utils::getS3method are imported explicitly.
  • Every exported function has runnable examples. The SIR model moved to inst/examples/sir_model.R so that examples, the vignette and users can all source it.
  • Two vignettes: Get started (an end-to-end SIR walkthrough) and Methods (Shapley weights, the Das Gupta equivalence, counterfactual types, sequential Shapley).
  • Tests register their toy methods with .S3method() instead of writing to .GlobalEnv with <<-. CRAN policy forbids modifying the user’s workspace.
  • shapley_decompose() reports progress with message() instead of cat(), so verbose = FALSE and suppressMessages() both silence it.
  • make_run_table() now prints when called at top level. It used to return directly after a :=, so its first auto-print was suppressed.
  • DESCRIPTION gains URL, BugReports, Depends: R (>= 4.0.0) (for .S3method), the parallel / utils imports and VignetteBuilder.
  • .Rbuildignore keeps manuscript/, .github/, _pkgdown.yml and scratch/ out of the tarball.
  • CI: R-CMD-check.yaml (macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu on devel / release / oldrel) and pkgdown.yaml.

3. Should fix before submitting

Done (2026-10-13): - ihme_loc_id grouping replaced by a group_vars argument (shapley_decompose(), run_decomp(), sequential_totals()). - The internal hiv_decomp reference removed from the future_policies docs. - DESCRIPTION rewritten, with references in CRAN form: Shapley (1953) doi:10.1515/9781400881970-018 (DOI verified against Crossref) and Das Gupta (1993) (URL verified). - The stale run-table comment fixed. - Spelling pass, with domain terms in inst/WORDLIST. URL check: all URLs correct. - Found along the way: the warm-start docs described a contract the code doesn’t follow. They now document what shapley_decompose() actually passes, with a runnable example. n_cores > 1 on Windows now falls back instead of erroring.

Still open (tracked as GitHub issues): - Run the external checks and submit (tracking issue). The maintainer email, aucarter@uw.edu, is confirmed (2026-10-21). - Give the full citation for the sequential-Shapley reference in the shapley_decompose() details. The Methods vignette cites a different title; the two should agree. - Rename \pkg{decomposer} in the manuscript, and add inst/CITATION once it has a DOI.

4. Submission steps

  1. Confirm the site deploys and the CI matrix is green. Done.
  2. Move the callers listed in 1.1 when convenient. CRAN does not need this.
  3. Work through section 3.
  4. Bump the version (suggest 1.0.0, given the API commitment) and update NEWS.md.
  5. Run the external checks: devtools::check_win_devel(), devtools::check_mac_release(), and rhub::rhub_check() for the additional platforms. Results come back by email.
  6. Update cran-comments.md with the check results and the “new submission” note.
  7. Run devtools::submit_cran(), then confirm the submission from the link CRAN emails to the maintainer.
  8. Expect one round of reviewer comments for a first submission (usually 1–3 weeks). Address them, bump the patch version, and resubmit.

Rough effort: about half a day (M) for section 3 and the submission, plus calendar time for CRAN’s review.

5. After acceptance

  • CRAN re-checks the package against every R-devel release. A failure comes with a deadline (typically 2–4 weeks) to fix it before the package is archived.
  • Every update goes through the same incoming checks, so batch changes into releases rather than pushing small ones.
  • Keep main installable from GitHub for the internal pipeline, and cut CRAN releases from tags.
